## Comparability caveat

Alaska Air Group's FY2024 figures are not on a fully comparable basis with the other four carriers: Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward, contributing $869 million of revenue (and a $113 million net loss) for the stub period [DOC-2]. Alaska's ratios therefore blend a full year of standalone Alaska with roughly 3.5 months of Hawaiian, whereas Delta, United, Southwest, and American reflect full-year continuing operations. All five are calendar-year filers (Jan 1 – Dec 31), so there is no fiscal-year mismatch [DOC-1]. Also note that cost-line labeling (e.g., what is captured in "salaries, wages and benefits" vs. other labor-related lines such as regional carrier expense or contract labor) can differ by filer, so small gaps between carriers should not be over-read.

## 1. Aircraft fuel expense as % of total operating revenue (lowest first)

| Rank | Airline | Fuel / Revenue | Calculation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | **17.1%** | $10,566M / $61,643M [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | **20.6%** | $11,756M / $57,063M [DOC-1] |
| 3 | American | **21.1%** | $11,418M / $54,211M [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | **21.1%** | $5,812M / $27,483M [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Alaska | **21.4%** | $2,506M / $11,735M [DOC-1] |

American (21.06%) and Southwest (21.15%) are effectively tied — the 9 basis-point gap is not meaningful.

## 2. Salaries, wages and benefits as % of total operating revenue (lowest first)

| Rank | Airline | Labor / Revenue | Calculation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | **26.2%** | $16,161M / $61,643M [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | **29.2%** | $16,678M / $57,063M [DOC-1] |
| 3 | American | **29.6%** | $16,021M / $54,211M [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Alaska | **30.6%** | $3,588M / $11,735M [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Southwest | **44.5%** | $12,240M / $27,483M [DOC-1] |

## 3. Is the top-ranked airline the same?

Yes — Delta ranks lowest on both metrics, with the lowest fuel intensity (17.1%) and the lowest labor intensity (26.2%), consistent with it also posting the highest operating income of the group at $5,995M [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Fuel % of revenue (lowest first): Delta 17.1%, United 20.6%, American 21.1%, Southwest 21.1%, Alaska 21.4%. Salaries/wages/benefits % of revenue (lowest first): Delta 26.2%, United 29.2%, American 29.6%, Alaska 30.6%, Southwest 44.5%. Yes — Delta is top-ranked (lowest) in both, though Alaska's ratios are not strictly comparable because Hawaiian is consolidated only from September 18, 2024.
